english.title: Employer / self employed person fail to give information to non-employees regarding health and safety

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Health and Safety at Work Act 1974

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being

(A)_[an employer,]_
(B)_[a self-employed person,]_

failed, in a case that was prescribed by **(..SPECIFY PRESCRIBING REGULATIONS..), to fulfil your duty, in the prescribed circumstances and manner to give to persons, not being your employees, who may be affected by the way in which you conducted your undertaking the prescribed information about such aspects of the way in which you conducted your undertaking as might affect their health and safety
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 3(3) and 33(1)(a) of, and Schedule 3A to, the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
employer / self-employed

to affected non-employees

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See section 2(2) of the Act for examples of the extent of the employer's duty.
(ii) Proceedings for an offence shall not, in England and Wales, be instituted except by an inspector of the Environment Agency or the Natural Resources Body for Wales or by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions, see section 38 of the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974.

other.penalty:
Either way -
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2002; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see schedule 3A to the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
